tells.1: Em dashes plus a promotional closer ('a practical way to get a fuller picture... make the most of their yearly checkup')
tells.2: Tidy closer 'a simple way to get the full picture', a stock marketing phrase
tells.3: Over-compressed and clipped, with a bare price line at the end
tells.4: Clean three-beat structure ('helps guide care as your dog ages') that feels slightly templated

reason: Version 5 reads like real clinic copy: it's a bit clunky and wordy ('highly beneficial', 'his vaccines'), so it's the most human but not the most polished. Version 4 keeps the same content in clear, credible language without the salesy filler of 1 and 2, so it's the one I'd publish.
